newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian cashewnut growers expect bumper harvest.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian cashewnut growers expect bumper harvest.

text.p: Tanzanian cashewnut growers expect a bumper harvest of 75,000 tonnes in 1996/97 compared to 55,000 tonnes for 1995/96, the privately-owned weekly Financial Times newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper cited officials within the Tanzania Cashewnut Marketing Board (TCMB) for the projections.

The TCMB official was quoted as saying that the state-owned body had no funds to buy the crop following the start of the buying season in October. The official said private traders paid 250-290 shillings per kg (2.205 lb) for cashewnuts compared to last season prices worth up to 450 shillings per kg.
The board has been embroiled in controversy following the dismissal earlier this year of two senior executives in connection with the missapropriation of TCMB funds.
TCMB statistics show that cashewnut production peaked in 1973/74 season with 145,000 tonnes harvested.
Tanzanian cashewnuts are mostly grown in the southern Mtwara region bordering Mozambique.
